frequency_question: How often do legislative principals successfully initiate and carry through a joint resolution of disapproval against a major international agreement when they possess the formal constitutional/statutory capability to do so?
membership_rule: Includes all joint resolutions of disapproval targeting major executive-branch arms sales or nuclear agreements where floor votes occurred; excludes simple resolutions that lacked bicameral statutory teeth.

cases.name: 2015 Iran Nuclear Agreement (JCPOA) resolution of disapproval

coverage_note: 3 major historical showdowns identified where legislative principals formally attempted to block major executive pacts.
known_gaps: Minor non-privileged resolutions or withdrawn resolutions are excluded as they never reached the threshold of active principal will and delivery.
skeleton: Legislative attempts to block major executive foreign/nuclear agreements through privileged joint resolutions since 1976.
multiplier: 1 successful override/passage blocking an agreement out of 3 major historical attempts where legislative will was tested.
validity_reason: The statutory framework governing congressional review of international arms and nuclear agreements remains stable under the AECA and Atomic Energy Act.
